title: Vampire checkpoint interrogation game
text: Builds a browser game where the player questions each arrival at a vampire checkpoint with five questions, then admits or rejects them, with three warnings ending the run.

title: Flappy Bird-inspired ball game
text: Builds a Flappy Bird-inspired ball game through conversational vibe coding and ships it as a playable website.

title: Unity game directed by repeated corrections
text: Directs a coding assistant through repeated corrections to produce a working Unity game, and writes up what vibecoding means for game development.

title: Open world safari game
text: Assembles an open-world safari game from terminal prompts and publishes it as a playable website.

title: Math game from a worksheet photo
text: Turns a photo of a kindergarten math worksheet into a playable browser math game in about ten minutes, then adds interface fixes after playtesting by the child.

title: Retro spelling game for a daughter
text: Builds a retro-styled spelling game for a nine-year-old where words are read aloud by text-to-speech and the player types them letter by letter.

title: Sand-chain block puzzle
text: Builds a Tetris-style puzzle where falling blocks leave sand particles that must connect across the screen to clear, and translates the site into several languages.

title: Multiplayer game played through coding tools
text: Builds a multiplayer game that players control from inside their coding tools through a tool-server interface.

title: Space Invaders with mascot theme
text: Builds a Space Invaders variant themed on a coding tool's mascot, with power-ups, combo multipliers and wave progression, playable in the browser.

title: Wrestling booking game
text: Builds a wrestling booking game in TypeScript over one week without reading any code, adding rankings, tournaments and a rating arcade.

title: Text adventure playing harness
text: Plays classic text adventures through a custom harness built at a hackathon, testing how a cognitive architecture helps with exploration and memory in interactive fiction.

title: Accelerometer marble game on old phone
text: Builds a WebGL marble game that uses the phone accelerometer, from a one-line spec typed on a four-year-old Android phone, in about three hours.

title: 3D multiplayer tank arena
text: Builds a 3D web multiplayer arena game where players buy tanks, helicopters, snipers and turrets to score points against a rival team.

title: Autonomous Minecraft player
text: Runs an autonomous Minecraft bot driven through a software development kit, so it plays the game on its own without a human at the controls.

title: Unity game creation from the command line
text: Creates Unity games from a command-line tool that drives the Unity project through a coding assistant, released as open source.

title: UFO abduction game with kids
text: Builds a browser UFO abduction game together with children as a family project, then publishes it as a free page playable on computers.

title: Overnight 3D golf game
text: Builds a 3D golf game in one evening using Svelte and Three.js, then publishes it as a playable website.

title: Original solitaire variant Confluence
text: Designs an original solitaire variant called Confluence and builds it alongside Klondike, Spider and other classic variants on a single browser page.

title: One hundred mini games from one prompt
text: Generates one hundred mini games from a single prompt in one coding session, then reports token use, duration and what worked.

title: Mario Galaxy-style 3D platformer
text: Builds a Mario Galaxy-style 3D web platformer with planets to run around, using Three.js, TypeScript and Rapier physics, over 53 days.

title: Hitster-style music card game from phone
text: Builds a Hitster-style music year-guessing card game from personal playlists in three to four hours, directed by voice messages from a phone during a car ride.

title: Browser MOBA with original champions
text: Builds a server-authoritative browser MOBA with two arenas, 18 original champions, jungle objectives, an item shop and bots.

title: Airport security queue sim
text: Builds an airport security queue simulation where the player manages checkpoints and shops while tracking served travelers, satisfaction and walk-offs.

title: Backrooms roguelike in 30 days
text: Vibe-codes a backrooms-themed roguelike in under 30 days and shares the finished game as a playable project.

title: Capybara game that earned revenue
text: Ships a capybara game built with a coding assistant and reports earning $25,000 within 15 days of release.

title: Game for rival assistants to fight in
text: Builds a simple game with a self-documenting hypermedia API and lets two rival coding assistants fight in it, scoring rounds by who keeps queueing actions.

title: CLI chess with assistant as wingman
text: Builds a command-line chess game in which the player gets a coding assistant as a wingman while playing.

title: WebGPU tank game with build rounds
text: Builds a browser WebGPU multiplayer tank game with round-by-round upgrade building, inspired by a WWII shooter and a hero shooter's build mode, with limited coding experience.

title: Starship text adventure teaching prompts
text: Builds a text adventure on a failing starship that teaches prompting, skills and autonomous agents through about eight minutes of play with real code samples.

title: Elite-style space trading game
text: Recreates an Elite-style space trading and combat game by vibe coding it as an open-source project.

title: Amiga game port to Godot
text: Ports a 1993 Amiga game to Godot by reading its original 68000 assembly to recover rules and behavior.

title: Coding sessions as a pixel adventure
text: Turns every coding session into a game with generative music that follows the session mood and a pixel knight who battles a monster per edit and command.

title: Vocabulary game from a Korean webtoon
text: Builds a top-down game for learning vocabulary from a Korean webtoon, with dialogue, a word journal, grammar notes and culture notes.

title: Making a game legible to coding tools
text: Restructures a game so its state and tooling are legible to coding assistants and automated iteration is faster, as covered in a conference talk.

title: Two-day online multiplayer game
text: Builds an online multiplayer game in two days using a terminal coding tool, then publishes it as a playable website.

title: Crapless craps from a phone
text: Builds a crapless craps game as a Flutter web app, vibe coded entirely from a phone and served as an installable page.

title: Asteroids written as a chat artifact
text: Writes an Asteroids game as a single in-chat web app from a two-prompt exchange, the second prompt fixing a runtime error.

title: Chess tournament between chat assistants
text: Pits several chat assistants against each other at chess in a small web app to compare newer reasoning versions with older ones.

title: Assistant coaching assistant at chess
text: Has one assistant coach another to play chess against a strong engine, exploring multi-assistant setups for improving play.

title: Startup operations simulation game
text: Builds a startup operations simulation game as a shareable in-chat artifact, then fixes a few issues and posts an updated link.

title: Factorio played through a learning environment
text: Plays Factorio through a learning environment, building factories that must produce items such as batteries per minute and manage complex logistics.

title: Pokemon-style play inside a coding tool
text: Emulates Pokemon-style gameplay inside a coding assistant by packaging the game logic as a reusable skill that runs in the terminal session.

title: Interactive fiction from free time
text: Writes an interactive fiction piece called Discontinuum, published as a playable web page, during an assistant's free time slot set aside for its own projects.

title: Hitori puzzle implementation
text: Implements the Hitori puzzle game in an autonomous coding mode after studying how an existing Linux version is architected, and publishes it to play online.

title: Minecraft building through a tool server
text: Builds structures in Minecraft by giving language-driven control to the game through a tool-server API.

title: NetHack played autonomously
text: Plays NetHack autonomously through a software development kit while a macOS app lets a viewer watch the run unfold.

title: Multiplayer game built without code
text: Builds a multiplayer game in four days without writing any code by hand, relying on prompts and generated code throughout.

title: Godot editor connected to a tool server
text: Connects an assistant to the Godot editor through a plugin and tool server so it can inspect and edit game scenes.

title: Pokemon Red run on a live stream
text: Plays Pokemon Red live on a public stream, reasoning through navigation and battles to progress through the game.

title: Pokemon Red compared across assistants
text: Runs three different assistants through Pokemon Red and compares how each navigates and gets stuck, in published research notes.

title: Starter kit for Pokemon runs
text: Publishes a starter kit for running an assistant through Pokemon, with the loop that sends game screens and receives button presses.

title: Tetris clock counting down to New Year
text: Builds a Tetris clock with falling blocks that counts down to New Year, described in a short build write-up.

title: Tetris played inside Emacs
text: Plays Tetris inside Emacs through Lisp REPL loops that expose the editor and its display to the assistant.

title: Daily series: Hangman
text: Builds a browser Hangman game as the second entry in a daily series of vibe-coded games.

title: Daily series: Pong Paralyzer
text: Builds a Pong variant called Pong Paralyzer as day nine of a daily series of vibe-coded games.

title: Daily series: emoji Mahjong
text: Builds an emoji Mahjong tile-matching game as day 15 of a daily series of vibe-coded games.

title: Multiplayer MUD with automated playtesters
text: Builds a multiplayer MUD-style dungeon game in Kotlin with a Ktor server and Compose client, using automated testers to QA and playtest it.

title: Match-3 puzzle game
text: Builds a match-3 fruit puzzle game with a terminal coding tool and publishes it as a web game.

title: Monty Hall three-door simulator
text: Builds a Monty Hall three-door game simulator in two hours as a novice, using a code editor with an assistant.
